messages:
maya: FYI ran through the minimal Next.js starter for onboarding and hit an SSR auth refresh issue on first load. :bug:
maya: Repro steps: clone repo, yarn dev, sign in with demo creds, open /dashboard then hard refresh.
maya: On server render we see a 401 from /api/session/refresh and the SDK's automatic retries/refresh don't run.
maya: Log snippet:
```
GET /api/session/refresh 401
Error: Unauthorized
    at fetch (node_modules/whatwg-fetch)
```
maya: Looks like the starter uses native global fetch in getServerSideProps so our server-side interceptors never attach.
ryan: hmm, is the fetch patch not applied in _app or a server entrypoint? thought devex added a node patch helper.
maya: not in this starter — it's intentionally minimal to keep deps small.
sam: repro'd locally. Confirmed: retry/refresh logic lives in sdk/interceptors and the starter's SSR path calls fetch directly. No retry.
sam: Quick workaround: patch node fetch early. e.g. in pages/_middleware.ts (or a top-level server entry):
```
import { patchNodeFetch } from '@redwood-inference/sdk/node';
patchNodeFetch(globalThis);
```
sam: That patches global fetch so SDK interceptors (retry + token refresh) run on SSR.
maya: Patch works for me locally, :thumbsup:. But I'm wary of recommending global patch in a teaching starter — could hide complexity.
sam: Agreed. Alternative minimal pattern to keep things explicit: create a server client and pass fetch in per-request so handlers opt-in:
```
import { createServerClient } from '@redwood-inference/sdk/server';
export async function getServerSideProps(ctx) {
  const client = createServerClient({ fetch: ctx.fetch ?? fetch });
  const user = await client.auth.getUser();
  return { props: { user } };
}
```
sam: That ensures the SDK uses the SSR fetch context and preserves retry behavior without global monkeypatching.
ryan: I like the explicit client approach — less magic for beginners. Also easier to test.
maya: can we add a tiny e2e that simulates an expired cookie and verifies refresh happens? simple Playwright step should catch regressions.
sam: yep. I'll add both examples to the starter (global patch note + explicit server client example) plus one Playwright test. Opening a PR now and will ping reviewers.
ci-bot: PR opened: #4822 by sam (devex) — includes server-client example, README note, and a Playwright e2e. CI checks running.
maya: awesome, thanks. I'll add a short paragraph in the README about SSR auth caveat and link to the SDK server-client helper snippet.
ryan: LGTM once CI is green. Please add a line to the changelog so customers know we tightened SSR guidance.
maya: will do.
